summary:
Checked all four W2 review findings against the code. R1 and R3 are fixed in code with tests. R2 is handled with option (a), documentation only, because option (b) contradicts the spec. R4 is real, but the file is not mine, so the exact fix is under needsOtherFiles.

W2-R1 (FIXED): backend/src/lib/moduleAccess.ts. GATED_PREFIXES now starts with `{ prefix: '/auth/integrations/whatsapp', anyOf: ['api_whatsapp'] }`, which gates GET, PUT and POST /test. /auth/integrations/delivery-status is still not gated, so the managers' banner keeps working. Test added to connectorsWhatsapp.test.ts: an `it` user with moduleDeny ['api_whatsapp'] gets 403 on GET, PUT (attacker URL) and /test, and the stored gateway URL does not change. The same user still gets 200 on delivery-status and on /connectors. A saved `it` role row without api_whatsapp also closes the route for the whole role. I did not do the optional CEO notification: the URL change is already audited (integrations.whatsapp.update), and a WhatsApp message would go out through the redirected gateway anyway.

W2-R3 (FIXED, no migration and no schema change): moduleAccess.ts now has `MODULE_GRANTS = ['api_pos','api_whatsapp','voided_prebills']`, `rolesGrantedByDefault(id)` and `applyModuleGrants()`.
- Which rows: the role list comes from DEFAULT_MODULE_ACCESS (non-admin), so it cannot drift. Today that is api_pos → it, management; api_whatsapp → it; voided_prebills → finance, management, owner.
- How: each row update is conditional (`updateMany where NOT modules has X, data push X`), so it is safe when several processes run it at once.
- Runs once ever: the marker `settings['moduleAccess.grantsApplied']` lists the grants already applied. If the CEO unticks a module later, it stays unticked. Roles with no saved row are not touched; they get the new modules from the defaults.
- When it runs: lazily, once per process, before the first override read. If it fails, it fails open and the next process tries again. A boot call in index.ts is still wanted (see needsOtherFiles), so the matrix GET shows the new modules from the first request.
- Test added: grants go to the right rows with no duplicates; a non-grantee row and a role with no row are unchanged; IT reaches /connectors and the WhatsApp routes after the grant; a re-run does nothing; a CEO untick sticks; concurrent runs do not duplicate ids.

W2-R2 (option (a), documentation only; (b) rejected): the binding spec §13 step 4 says lib/whatsapp.ts re-encrypts a plaintext key on first read, and §14 tests it. Moving encryption to the next save would break both, so I kept re-encrypt-on-read and documented the rollback hazard:
- docs/TAX_SETUP.md §4 step 0 and a new troubleshooting row: re-enter the key in the old /configuration/whatsapp screen. That page exists at HEAD.
- CLAUDE.md: a new bullet in the POS connector section, plus one sentence in the SERVD_SECRET_KEY deploy-secret row.
- A comment in lib/whatsapp.ts.
- Spec §12 is not my file; the line to add is under needsOtherFiles.
I also added a TAX_SETUP troubleshooting row for "IT gets 403 on Dev → API pages".

W2-R4 (real, not my file): `infra/staging.tfvars.example` is outside the files I own (I own infra/main.tf and infra/prod.tfvars.example), so I did not edit it.

tsc --noEmit is clean, and the four test files pass (58 tests).
tests: cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit -p . is clean. Ran vitest on tests/connectorsWhatsapp.test.ts, tests/whatsappConfig.test.ts, tests/workspaces.test.ts and tests/accessControl.test.ts against servd_test_w2_build with the given env: 4 files and 58 tests pass. New tests in connectorsWhatsapp.test.ts: (1) 'the CEO's per-user deny closes the WhatsApp gateway routes too (W2-R1), not the delivery banner'; (2) a describe block 'new default modules reach saved Module Access rows once (W2-R3)', which checks which roles get each grant, applying the grants once, the CEO untick sticking, and concurrent runs not duplicating ids.
deviations:
- W2-R2: I chose option (a), documentation only, and rejected (b). The binding spec §13 step 4 and the §14 test list require re-encrypt-on-first-read.
- W2-R3: instead of a data-only migration (the migrations directory is not mine), I built an idempotent reconcile in moduleAccess.ts. It runs once, tracked by a marker in `settings`, and is triggered lazily per process; a boot call is still needed in index.ts (see needsOtherFiles). Result: CEO unticks made after the grant are kept, which a plain migration would also do.
- W2-R4: not edited, because the file is outside the files I own; the exact replacement is under needsOtherFiles.
- W2-R1: the optional notification to the CEO when the gateway URL changes was not implemented; the change is already audited.
